note: Forest Service campground near Davisville, rebuilt in 2023 on high ground above the Huzzah Creek floodplain: paved roads and spurs in the Ridge Top and Creek loops, both with 30/50A pedestals, plus a group loop and the small non-electric Pines Overlook loop. The creek, with its gravel bars and red bluffs, is a walk down from the Creek Loop; no site is on it. Flash flooding is possible along the creek. One-mile Red Bluff Trail. --Claude
summary: Closed for the season in the ordinary way (2026 season ended October 26; 2027 opens April 24). The entry describes the campground before its 2023 rebuild: it now has 48 single sites (41 electric with 30/50A, 7 non-electric), not '44 sites (6 electric)', all on high ground. $25 electric / $15 non-electric as stored. Note rewritten; season, sites, facilities, booking written. Creekside no longer holds - lead down. Pin is across the creek from every loop - move flagged. policy_ref missing.
flags: REBUILT CAMPGROUND: recreation.gov's overview says 'Three new camping loops were constructed above the Huzzah Creek floodplain - Ridge Top Loop, Creek Loop, and Group Loop - each of which have modern restrooms, water, and electricity' (2023), with 'a new shower house, a dump station, and second pavilion', and the fourth loop, Pines Overlook, renovated but non-electric. The stored note ('44 sites (6 electric) with some sites close to the creek') describes the old layout.

WATERFRONT DOWN (stored creekside; lead: not waterfront): per-site coordinates on leaf-off imagery. The Creek Loop's nearest sites (CL1-CL5) are on a terrace 60-80 m from Huzzah Creek with a wooded slope and the floodplain between; the rest of the loop is 100-200 m back. The Ridge Top, Group and Pines Overlook loops are on a ridge 700 m to the south-west, 150-400 m from the creek's next bend and well above it. recreation.gov's summer photos of CL2, CL3 and CL4 show the pads backed by solid woods with no water in sight, and its own text says 'Many sites are within 200 yards of Huzzah Creek'. The catalog tags three Ridge Top sites (RTL1, RTL18, RTL23) 'Riverfront', which the coordinates contradict - they are 250 m or more from the water. Huzzah Creek is about 15-25 m wide here. Nothing is within 50 m and no view can be shown, so the value goes down to not waterfront.

PIN MOVE: stored 37.8164,-91.1664 is recreation.gov's facility point; on imagery it falls in timber on the far (north-east) side of Huzzah Creek, about 330 m from the nearest site. Loop centres from the per-site coordinates: Ridge Top Loop 37.81223,-91.17682 (with the Group Loop and Pines Overlook beside it - 41 of the site records are in this cluster, at the entrance from Highway V); Creek Loop 37.81433,-91.16937. Suggested pin: Ridge Top Loop, 37.81223,-91.17682 (about 1.0 km west-south-west of the stored pin).
POLICY ROW: the entry has no policy_ref; it is a Mark Twain National Forest campground (Potosi-Fredericktown Ranger District) and should carry federal:usfs.

ELECTRIC BY SITE: catalog amperage - Creek Loop 19 sites '50'; Ridge Top Loop 13 sites '30/50', 5 sites '30', the rest '50'; Pines Overlook none (the catalog's '50' on those records contradicts the facility text and their NONELECTRIC type, and they are sold at the non-electric rate).

RIG LENGTH: Max Vehicle Length is 40 ft on 56 of 62 records, 35 ft on two and 30 ft on one; nothing under 23 ft. No rig-length wording singles the campground out ('Camping spurs are variable in size and layout to accommodate recreational vehicles and trailers of all types').
SEASON: stored 'about May to October' (derived, approximate) replaced by the rate-table dates. Whether any loop stays open without services in winter I could not read.
BOOKING: reservations close 4 days before arrival (reservationCutOff rule); 8 sites are first come, first served. 3-night minimum on holiday weekends only.
STATUS: no closure or flood-damage notice on the recreation.gov record (only the standing 'Flash flooding is possible in the area'). Forest alerts were not read.

UNREAD: the Forest Service page - https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/marktwain/recreation/red-bluff-campground returned 404 and I did not hunt for the new address; forest alerts and orders unread. Everything is from recreation.gov and imagery.
